mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to expected future cash flows, lowering the present value of equities and thus producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in such regimes are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) in a 5-year walk-forward test.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in unemployment claims accompanied by a decline in the monthly Payroll Employment Change (PAYEMS) signals weakening labor market strength, which tends to depress consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls by > 10,000 jobs while UNRATE rises by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: In 80% of similar labor-market-softening events, the 20-day forward return is non-negative (quantile regression).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCP) surprise turns positive by more than 0.5% above consensus and persists for two months, it indicates accelerating consumer demand, which elevates earnings growth expectations and pushes S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PCP surprise > +0.5% for two consecutive months (proxy: GDPC1 surprise > +1.0%)
failure_condition: Over 50 similar positive surprises, the 5-day forward return mean is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in Industrial Production (INDPRO) of more than 2% month-over-month, followed by a sustained decline in the RSAFS (order backlog), predicts reduced manufacturing capacity utilization and thus negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > -2% and RSAFS falls > -10% in the same month
failure_condition: In 40 such contraction events, the 20-day forward return median is positive (quantile).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the UNRATE below 5% for three consecutive months indicates labor market tightening, prompting the Federal Reserve to hold rates steady but reducing growth expectations and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during such regimes are not statistically lower than during expansion (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly PAYEMS exceeds 130,000 by a surprise of +20,000 and UNRATE simultaneously falls below 7%, it signals a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate optimism, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In 30 such events, the 20-day forward return mean is not positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the CPIAUCSL inflation rate above 3% for two consecutive months triggers a preemptive hike in the FEDFUNDS rate, which compresses equity discount rates and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: In 40 such inflation spikes, the 5-day forward return is not negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in both GDPC1 (goods orders) and HOUST (housing starts) by at least 10% in the same month suggests a dual softening in business and residential demand, which lowers growth expectations and results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < -10% and HOUST < -10% in the same month
failure_condition: In 25 such events, the 20-day forward return mean is not negative (p > 0.05).
